# Handoff — r10 defect fixes mid-render; startup restructured; planet scenes prepped
Written: 2026-07-25 20:45 · Session: ~45 turns

## Where things stand

A **full 51-scene asset re-render is RUNNING** in a screen session Rick owns
(`python3 scripts/rerender_all.py --clean-cache`, sky recipe **r10**, HEIC quality 0.95).
It was at **11/49** at handoff time, ~3 h left. A second background job is re-rendering
four object scenes that r10 initially broke — sombrero and m106 are done and verified,
m8_lagoon and potm2508a still going (`/tmp/objfix.log`).

Alongside that, four app changes landed and **all build clean** but only ONE is verified on
device. Nothing is committed. Planet-scene assets (Iapetus / Jupiter / Saturn / Venus) are
downloaded and upscaled but no scene-building work has started.

## Decisions made (and why)

**The pod "completion" race — fixed in THREE places, this is the big one.**
`sky360._run`, `process_backdrops.depth_via_comfy` and `neural_sr._run_pod` all submitted a
ComfyUI job then polled `/queue` until idle, then took `ls -t <tag>_*.png | head -1`. The
queue can read empty *before* ComfyUI registers a just-POSTed prompt, so the first poll
breaks immediately and `ls -t` copies the **previous run's output for that scene** — silently,
in ~1s, all the way through to a packed HEIC. Observed live on carina_mystic. All three now
snapshot the output listing *before* submitting and wait for a filename they have not seen.
`neural_sr` was the worst-placed because `sr_equirect` runs on every scene against tags that
accumulate files across every previous render. **If you add another pod stage, use this
pattern.** A ~1s stage time is the tell.

**`kind` is measured, but fov is a missing term in that rule.** `potm_auto_manifest.border_level`
(brightest of four edge medians) was applied to the 9 hand rows for the first time; four were
wrong. m31 (border 143) and ngc4631_whale (51) became `field` — that fixed the "images stacked
on top of each other" report at its root, since the object recipe had been painting a *second*
galaxy. But m8_lagoon (border 1.3) was moved to `object` and that made it **worse** — a circular
porthole. At fov 144 the footprint spans most of the forward view, so a hard-bounded fill reads
as a porthole rather than a hero in the void. It is back to `field`. The measurement is a good
proxy for narrow objects and a bad one at large fov.

**The object fill must have NO distance falloff.** This was my regression and it broke every
object scene (sombrero, m106, m8_lagoon, potm2508a → glowing portholes). A flat fill is uniform
over the whole sphere so there is no boundary for diffusion to find; dimming it toward a floor
creates a bounded disc of lighter sky that the outpaint develops into a rimmed halo. It was
added to stop m31 washing grey, but m31's real problem was being mis-typed. **Fields keep the
falloff — that is where it was needed and verified (potm2307a).**

**Do not change several things at once mid-render.** Two separate regressions this session came
from batching changes and then having to untangle which caused what.

**Blender earns its place only on Saturn's rings.** `CustomMaterial` is unavailable on visionOS
(Xcode rejects it in xrOS) — only `ShaderGraphMaterial` from Reality Composer Pro, no hand-written
Metal. So built-in shadows can't give the ring shadow band on the globe or the globe's shadow
across the rings. Plan: model in Blender, ray-trace in Cycles, **bake the shadowing into
textures**, export USDZ, load as real geometry in RealityKit. Bake the *lighting*, never the
*geometry* — stereo parallax must stay real. Frozen lighting is fine for a body that rotates
once per 10.6 h.

**Planets/moons go in as geometry, not baked into the equirect.** The backdrop sits at one
near-infinite depth (`depth_floor 0.94`, 0.22% baseline), so anything pasted there has no
parallax — a large part of why saturn1 reads as a picture.

**"Huge" and "sharp" trade against each other.** Filling more view means you're closer, seeing
less surface magnified more. Required cylindrical map width ≈ `360 × 34 px/deg × R/(d−R)`:
30°→4.3K, 40°→6.4K, 50°→9K, 60°→12.2K, 80°→22K, 90°→29.5K. Iapetus (11741 real) is crisp to
~59°; Venus (8192 real) to ~47°; Saturn/Jupiter are only 4096 *real* under an 8192 SR, so honest
detail runs out ~29°. **Saturn's escape:** the rings span ~2.3× the globe radius, so the ring
system can fill 80–90° while the globe subtends 35–40°.

**Starfield per scene = yaw-only rotation.** Baked stereo disparity is horizontal in equirect
space with a pole falloff; any pitch/roll tilts it off the interocular axis → vertical disparity
→ nauseating. Yaw alone gives plenty of variety. Measured on `deep_star_map`: forward-view
brightness swings 6× across yaw. Four well-separated angles: **165°** sparse (mean 0.31),
**0°** band high +12° (0.36), **105°** band level (0.93), **255°** dense galactic centre (1.91).
Use `deep_star_map` (real Gaia/Tycho, HDR EXR, already in pipeline), not the Solar System Scope
8k_stars — same 8192×4096 but an 8-bit artist JPEG.

**Splash freeze was never the animation's fault.** `SplashView` derives phase from
`context.date`, so a blocked main thread *freezes* it and then jumps. First fix attempt moved
only the file read off-main and did NOT work, because `CGImageSourceCreateImageAtIndex` returns
a **lazy** CGImage — the decode deferred until `TextureResource` touched the pixels, back on
main. `kCGImageSourceShouldCacheImmediately: true` is what actually relocates the cost.

## Files touched

- `upscale/sky360.py` — **SKY_RECIPE = "r10"**. Edge-clamp fill replacing mirror-tiling (killed
  the m8 triptych + black gutters); far-field seed texture is now seeded noise, not the master's
  own texture (measured: mirror-tiled fine detail carried p2p 80 in the flank vs 10 for the
  blurred far field — it was doing most of the ghosting); `FAR_FALLOFF_DEG` (degrees, not
  fraction-of-width — a wide pano and a narrow object need the same *angular* ramp);
  `FLOOR_PCTL=2` + `FLOOR_GAIN=0.5` (wall-to-wall starfield masters have no dark sky at all —
  potm2307a's 1st percentile is 13 — so the floor must go below anything in frame);
  `FOOT_EXPONENT=4` superellipse footprint via `footprint_alpha()`; object branch flat fill
  restored; `_run` race fix; `_mirror_map` deleted.
- `upscale/deepsky_pipeline.py` — measured `kind` on the 9 hand rows (m31/whale → field, m8 →
  field after the porthole, m106 stays object as the one ambiguous case at border 26.3);
  sombrero_wrap row removed; `_paste_master` uses the shared `footprint_alpha`;
  `FLOAT_SKY_CACHE` env override.
- `upscale/stereo_synth.py` — **sub-pixel forward warp.** `round()` quantised disparity to whole
  pixels; with `cos²(lat)` sweeping half-disparity 13.5→0 that carved **13 integer terraces per
  hemisphere at fixed latitudes on every scene**, content-independent. That is the "banding"
  Rick marked on spherex_stars. Also fixed a **pre-existing** inverted z-priority: the sort key
  was signed disparity, so the right eye (negative) let the *far* surface win contested pixels.
  Key is now `|disp|`.
- `upscale/neural_sr.py`, `upscale/process_backdrops.py` — pod race fix.
- `upscale/master_sr.py` — `SR_BACKEND` defaults to **esrgan** (plain RealESRGAN_x4plus, no
  tiling/seam-fix/sampler); USDU kept as `FLOAT_MASTER_SR=usdu` with its Band Pass seam fix
  turned off. Added `--redo` (re-SR masters already in `potm_sr/`, in place, atomic rename, and
  re-fetches originals from `potm_manifest.json`). Measured: USDU manufactured **3.6× the edge
  roughness** of a plain resample on saturn1's limb (7.95 vs 2.23) to close a 1.25× shortfall.
- `scripts/rerender_all.py` — **NEW, untracked.** Two-phase runner, live progress bar + ETA,
  resumable state journal, preflight, `--clean-cache`, scratch relocation.
- `Float/Layers/DepthLayers.swift` — transition fades to **black** via one `FADE_TINT` constant
  used by both the per-frame tint and the initial material. Type names still say "Whiteout"
  deliberately (renaming would have collided with a concurrent agent) — worth renaming now.
- `Float/App/AppModel.swift` — `recenter()` (yaw-only, snaps, returns Bool), `preparedSky`,
  `prepareFirstSky()`, Recenter button, `.opening` set *before* the decode.
- `Float/Immersive/ImmersiveView.swift` — world-tracking session; launch auto-recenter (retries
  until tracked, 3 s bound); consumes `preparedSky` synchronously.
- `Float/Immersive/SpatialImageEnvironment.swift` — `load` split into `prepare` + `attach`;
  decode AND texture creation both detached; `kCGImageSourceShouldCacheImmediately`.
- `Float/App/SplashView.swift` — "LOADING STARMAPS…" status line above the hairline.
- `Float/Interaction/Interaction.swift` — Recenter in `ControlPanelView`.
- `triage.html` — sombrero_wrap card removed surgically (regenerating would wipe Rick's
  KEEP/REMOVE tags). 50 cards, all with thumbnails.
- `Float/Resources/Textures/_raw/potm` → **symlink** to `/Volumes/Logic Pro/FloatScratch/raw_potm`.

## What's verified vs assumed

VERIFIED by measurement or build:
- **BUILD SUCCEEDED** after every app change (`xcodegen generate` && `xcodebuild -scheme Float
  -destination 'generic/platform=visionOS'`). SourceKit diagnostics in this repo are noise (it
  resolves against macOS); the build is the only truth.
- Stereo terracing: 26 terrace rows → 0 on a synthetic probe; on the real spherex image the
  old-vs-new disagreement ramps monotonically 0.34→1.82 with fractional disparity, the exact
  signature of removing quantisation. Silhouettes stay crisp (0 px transition on a 40 px step),
  disocclusion still background-filled, both eyes.
- m8 ghost energy: flank p2p 80 → 16 after edge-clamp + noise seed.
- Sombrero after the object fix: radial profile 46 → 0.22 → 0.00, no rim plateau.
- saturn1 source is **2586×1454** (LZW-compressed; an earlier file-size estimate of ~1100 px was
  wrong), upscaled only 1.44×.
- **Recenter works perfectly on device** (Rick confirmed).

ASSUMED / NOT VERIFIED:
- Black transition fade, off-main decode, preload restructure, "Loading starmaps…" — none seen
  in the headset. Specifically unknown: whether the splash now animates smoothly. If it still
  stutters, remaining suspects are the ShaderGraph material load or RealityKit's internal
  main-thread work during upload — that needs **Instruments on device**, not more guessing.
- The 38 scenes not yet re-rendered.
- Blender ring bake — planned, nothing built.

## Next step

**Wait for the render, then headset pass.** Everything queued behind it depends on what Rick
sees. Specifically watch: `weic2427a` (fov 239), `weic2615a` (193), `bullet-cluster` (191) —
the widest `object` scenes, closest to where m8's porthole lived. They *should* be fine with the
flat fill restored, but they are the untested edge.

Then, in order:
1. `python3 upscale/master_sr.py --redo` (8 masters need re-SR off the condemned USDU recipe;

2. Build the four planet scenes (assets ready in `/Volumes/Logic Pro/FloatScratch/planets/`:

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md

- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md

## claude.ai Zapier
This server connects you to 9,000+ apps via Zapier.

IMPORTANT: Before calling any tool, ensure you have loaded the available tools from this server (tools/list).

If the user seems new or has no tools enabled, retrieve the "zapier-mcp-onboarding" skill using get_zapier_skill and follow its instructions.
Use list_zapier_skills to discover other saved workflows.

## Managing what's enabled

- `inspect_zapier_actions({ selected_api?, action?, tool_name?, params? })` — inspect enabled actions and resolve action parameter schemas. **Returns everything you need to build an execute call**: each action's `app` (display name), `selected_api`, `action` key, `action_type` (exact SDK type), `tool_name`, `params`, inline dynamic enum values when resolvable, and `dynamic_properties_schema` when parent values in `params` are sufficient.
- `discover_zapier_actions({ app? })` — search the Zapier app catalog for actions to enable (`app` is a free-text search query).
- `enable_zapier_action({ selected_api, app_display_name?, action? })` — add an action (you'll receive a `tools/list_changed` notification afterwards). Pass the `selected_api` returned by `discover_zapier_actions`.
- `disable_zapier_action({ selected_api, app_display_name?, action? })` — remove an action. Pass the `selected_api` from `inspect_zapier_actions`.

## Executing an action

Always call `inspect_zapier_actions` first to retrieve the action's exact `selected_api`, `action` key, `tool_name`, parameter schema, and any dynamic-argument guidance. Then:

1. If a parameter has `dynamic_enum_values`, use one of those `value` fields. If it has `dynamic_enum_missing_dependencies` or no usable value yet, set the dependency params you know and call `inspect_zapier_actions({ tool_name, params })` again. Use `enum_property`, `enum_search`, and `enum_cursor` with the same tool when you need to search or page one dynamic enum.
2. If the action includes `dynamic_properties_depends_on`, settle those parameters' values, then call `inspect_zapier_actions({ tool_name, params })` … [truncated]

- handoff: Write a handoff document that lets the current work continue in a fresh session, then clear. Use when a session has grown long or expensive, when the Stop hook nudges about session length, at a natural task boundary, or whenever the user asks for a handoff, to "wrap up this session", or to start fresh without losing context.
- supacode-cli: Control Supacode from the terminal. Use when running Supacode CLI commands, managing worktrees, tabs, and surfaces programmatically, or when inside a Supacode terminal session.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). 202	    /// Extract the left (CGImage 0) and right (CGImage 1) eyes from the bundled spatial HEIC,
203	    /// **off the main actor**.
204	    ///
205	    /// This used to be a synchronous call from `@MainActor` code, which was a real stall, not
206	    /// a micro-optimisation: `CGImageSourceCreateImageAtIndex` decodes without suspending, and
207	    /// these are two 12288x6144 frames — ~300 MB of pixels each. On the main actor that blocks
208	    /// every frame for the duration, so SplashView's `TimelineView(.animation)` could not tick
209	    /// and its animation froze and jumped. Nothing in here touches actor-isolated state, so it
210	    /// is safe on a detached task; the main actor now just awaits the result and stays live.
211	    private static func loadEyes(name: String) async throws -> EyePair {
212	        try await Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated) {
213	            // kCGImageSourceShouldCacheImmediately is the whole point of this options dict.
214	            // Without it CGImageSourceCreateImageAtIndex returns a LAZY CGImage: it hands
215	            // back a descriptor and defers the actual decode until something first touches
216	            // the pixels — which is inside TextureResource, back on the main actor. So the
217	            // first attempt at moving this work off-main moved only the file read, and the
218	            // 75-megapixel-per-eye decode still landed on the main thread and still froze
219	            // SplashView. Forcing the decode HERE is what actually relocates the cost.
220	            let opts: [CFString: Any] = [kCGImageSourceShouldCacheImmediately: true]
221	            guard let url = Bundle.main.url(forResource: name, withExtension: "heic"),
222	                  let src = CGImageSourceCreateWithURL(url as CFURL, nil),
223	                  CGImageSourceGetCount(src) >= 2,
224	                  let left  = CGImageSourceCreateImageAtIndex(src, 0, opts as CFDictionary),
225	                  let right = CGImageSourceCreateImageAtIndex(src, 1, opts as CFDictionary)
226	            else { throw SpatialError.eyesUnavailable }
227	            return EyePair(left: left, right: right)
228	        }.value
229	    }

**BUILD SUCCEEDED.** (The SourceKit diagnostics are the usual noise in this repo — it resolves against macOS; `#Preview(windowStyle:)` and `RealityKitContent` both compile fine for xrOS.)

What changed in `Float/App/SplashView.swift`:

- **`TimelineView(.animation)` is gone.** No ripple expansion, no mote pulse, no vertical drift, no sweeping progress hairline.
- **The composition survives as a still frame.** The three ripple rings are rendered frozen at phases 0.16 / 0.49 / 0.82 of the old expansion curve, so it keeps the layered-ripple silhouette rather than collapsing to a bare circle. Guide ring, mote, starfield, FLOAT, and tagline are unchanged.
- **The progress hairline is deleted, not frozen.** A stationary bar reads as a stalled bar — worse than nothing. The status line ("LOADING STARMAPS…") now carries that job alone, moved up to where the hairline sat.
- The doc comment says plainly that this is static on purpose and why, so it doesn't get animated back.

I also corrected the comment in `SpatialImageEnvironment.swift:208` that justified the off-main decode by pointing at the splash animation — that animation no longer exists, but the off-main decode is still worth keeping on its own merits.

On "easy fix": there wasn't one. The decode is already off the main actor with `kCGImageSourceShouldCacheImmediately`, so what remains is RealityKit's texture upload doing main-thread work the app can't relocate. Every value in that view was driven by the main run loop, so anything animated there freezes and jumps for exactly as long as the upload blocks. Confirming which RealityKit call it is would need Instruments on device, and it wouldn't change the outcome for the splash either way.

Not verified in the headset — worth a look on your next device pass, alongside the black transition fade and the preload restructure that are still unseen.

1	import RealityKit
2	import UIKit
3	
4	// §7b transition flash — a brief full-view fade that masks a scene change. Kept from the
5	// (now retired) generated L1–L4 pipeline because the spatial-image scene system still uses
6	// it to mask a jump/select between skies. Everything else that lived here — the generated
7	// far backdrop, L2 nebula (splat/particle), L3 star volume, L4 phenomena — was removed when
8	// the app moved to a pre-rendered stereo-image library (see SpatialImageEnvironment).
9	// Fades to BLACK, not white (device round 7). A white flash masks a change by
10	// saturating, but between two dark deep-space scenes it reads as a jolt — the eye is
11	// dark-adapted and gets slammed to full brightness and back. Black masks just as
12	// completely (alpha 1 fully occludes either way) and costs the viewer nothing.
13	// Type names still say "Whiteout" so this stays a one-file change; see FADE_TINT.
14	struct WhiteoutComponent: Component {
15	    var active = false
16	    var elapsed: TimeInterval = 0
17	    var fadeIn: TimeInterval = 0.25
18	    var hold: TimeInterval = 0.12
19	    var fadeOut: TimeInterval = 0.45
20	    var total: TimeInterval { fadeIn + hold + fadeOut }
21	}
22	
23	/// 0 = black, 1 = white. One constant, used by both the per-frame tint and the initial
24	/// material, so they can never disagree.
25	let FADE_TINT: CGFloat = 0
26	
27	struct WhiteoutSystem: System {
28	    static let query = EntityQuery(where: .has(WhiteoutComponent.self))
29	    init(scene: Scene) {}
30	    func update(context: SceneUpdateContext) {
31	        MainActor.assumeIsolated {
32	            for e in context.entities(matching: Self.query, updatingSystemWhen: .rendering) {
33	                guard var c = e.components[WhiteoutComponent.self], c.active,
34	                      let me = e as? ModelEntity else { continue }
35	                c.elapsed += context.deltaTime
36	                var a: Float
37	                if c.elapsed < c.fadeIn {
38	                    a = Float(c.elapsed / c.fadeIn)                                   // fade to black
39	                } else if c.elapsed < c.fadeIn + c.hold {
40	                    a = 1                                                            // peak (swap happens here)
41	                } else if c.elapsed < c.total {
42	                    a = Float(1 - (c.elapsed - c.fadeIn - c.hold) / c.fadeOut)         // reveal new env
43	                } else {
44	                    a = 0; c.active = false
45	                }
46	                a = max(0, min(1, a))
47	                var mat = UnlitMaterial()
48	                mat.color = .init(tint: UIColor(white: FADE_TINT, alpha: CGFloat(a)), texture: nil)
49	                mat.blending = .transparent(opacity: 1.0)
50	                me.model?.materials = [mat]
51	                e.components[WhiteoutComponent.self] = c
52	            }
53	        }
54	    }
55	
56	    // Inward sphere just inside all content; alpha 0 until a jump/select flashes it (§7b).
57	    @MainActor
58	    static func makeEntity() -> ModelEntity {
59	        var mat = UnlitMaterial()
60	        mat.color = .init(tint: UIColor(white: FADE_TINT, alpha: 0), texture: nil)
61	        mat.blending = .transparent(opacity: 1.0)
62	        let e = ModelEntity(mesh: .generateSphere(radius: 1.5), materials: [mat])
63	        e.name = "Whiteout"
64	        e.scale.z = -1   // render the inside
65	        e.components.set(WhiteoutComponent())
66	        return e
67	    }
68	}

55	    /// `ImmersiveView` consumes this once and clears it; nil afterwards, and nil if the

57	    var preparedSky: ModelEntity?

60	    /// Ordering matters more than it looks: opening the space first and loading into it
61	    /// afterwards leaves the user staring into an empty black sphere for the length of a
62	    /// ~100 MB stereo HEIC decode. Doing it in this order costs the same wall time but
63	    /// spends it on a screen that has something to look at.
64	    func prepareFirstSky() async {
65	        guard preparedSky == nil else { return }

67	    }

69	    // MARK: - Recenter

72	    /// Session-only — deliberately not persisted, and deliberately NOT reset by a scene
73	    /// change: it describes which way the user's body is pointing, not which sky is up.
74	    /// Living on the persistent `sceneRoot` container means a swap inherits it for free.
75	    private(set) var recenterYaw: Float = 0
76	
77	    /// Make the direction the user is currently facing the scene's forward direction.
78	    ///
79	    /// **Yaw only.** Only the Y-axis component of the head pose is used; pitch and roll are
80	    /// discarded. The backdrop is a stereo 360 sphere whose per-eye disparity is baked
81	    /// horizontally in equirect space, so rotating content about any other axis tilts that
82	    /// baked disparity axis off the viewer's interocular axis and introduces vertical
83	    /// disparity — nauseating, not merely wrong-looking (§9, comfort is a gate).
84	    ///
85	    /// **Snaps, never animates.** Slewing the whole visual field is a textbook vection
86	    /// trigger; an instant cut is the comfortable option (§9). The camera does not move —
87	    /// only scene content rotates.
88	    /// Returns whether the recenter was actually applied. The launch auto-recenter polls on
89	    /// this: the device anchor is not tracked the instant the provider starts, so "did it
90	    /// take" has to be answerable rather than silently no-op.
91	    @discardableResult
92	    func recenter() -> Bool {
93	        guard let sceneRoot,
94	              let device = worldTracking?.queryDeviceAnchor(atTimestamp: CACurrentMediaTime()),
95	              device.isTracked
96	        else { return false }
97	
98	        // Head forward is the -Z column of the device transform. Keep only its horizontal
99	        // (x, z) part — that projection IS the yaw-only extraction.
100	        let m = device.originFromAnchorTransform
101	        let forward = SIMD2<Float>(-m.columns.2.x, -m.columns.2.z)
102	        // Degenerate when looking near-straight up or down: there is no meaningful facing
103	        // direction, so ignore the press rather than snap to an arbitrary heading.
104	        guard simd_length_squared(forward) > 1e-6 else { return false }
105	
106	        // forward == (-sin θ, -cos θ) for a yaw of θ about +Y.
107	        recenterYaw = atan2(-forward.x, -forward.y)
108	        // Composes with (does not replace) the sphere's canonical -90° facing, which lives
109	        // on the child ModelEntity in SpatialImageEnvironment.makeSphere().
110	        sceneRoot.orientation = simd_quatf(angle: recenterYaw, axis: [0, 1, 0])
111	        return true

content.text:
**BUILD SUCCEEDED.** (SourceKit's "cannot find in scope" spray is the usual noise — it lost the module index; the compiler resolves all of it.)

The diagnosis was a timing race, not a colour problem. `maskedSwap` slept a fixed 0.30 s, called the swap, and returned — but the swap only *started* an async decode taking seconds. The flash meanwhile ran its fixed 0.82 s course and faded out on schedule, uncovering the sphere that was still mounted (the old sky). Seconds later the decode landed and `attach` cut to the new sky with no mask left. Exactly the three beats you saw: black → original → jump.

The fix makes the mask outlast the work instead of guessing at its duration:

- **`WhiteoutComponent.holding`** (`Float/Layers/DepthLayers.swift`) — while set, the overlay parks at full black and its clock is clamped to the end of `hold`, so release always drops straight into the fade-out no matter how long the wait ran. `hold` is now a *minimum*, not the whole peak.
- **`maskedSwap(to:)`** (`Float/App/AppModel.swift`) — kicks off `prepare(index:)` at the same instant as the fade-in, awaits it, waits for the overlay to actually be opaque, attaches, then clears `holding`. The reveal is now driven by the load finishing.
- The opacity wait polls the component's own `elapsed` rather than sleeping 0.25 s of wall clock, since the flash advances on the render clock — that mismatch is what made the original fixed sleep fragile in the first place.
- A failed load (`prepare` returns nil) still releases, fading back to the current sky rather than parking at black.
- `selectScene` now checks "swap in flight" *before* writing `currentScene`/UserDefaults. The in-flight window is a full decode now, so a second tap during it would previously have persisted a sky that never loaded.

One consequence worth deciding on: a scene change now sits at full black for the entire decode — seconds, not 0.82 s. That's the honest cost; the old version only felt shorter because it showed you the wrong sky. If that hold turns out to feel too long in the headset, the lever is the same one behind the splash stutter — the decode itself — and options there are pre-decoding the *next* sky speculatively, or putting a status line on the black the way the splash now does.

Still unverified on device, along with the static splash.

The transition isn't long enough to worry about putting status text up. Consider this closed. Commit & push.

Next up, while I get up and walk away for food, I want you to work on the entertainment area. First of all, I want the web viewer we have embedded for my Kindle viewer to become an embedded browser that people can use to browse the web. It should default to open to the last page used, which in my case will be the Kindle, and it should have the ability to have tabs, pull up history, and load iCloud tabs. Second, the Music integration just quits the app and opens the Music app. It needs to have an embedded interface. Same with the video. It should open up a window where you can select something from your TV app library to watch. Other streaming services can be gotten through the web browser, so maybe we relabel the button to make it clear where the content is coming from.

Fix splash stutter, scene-swap race; sky recipe r10; pod completion race

App:
- SplashView is now static. Its ripple/mote/drift/sweep all derived phase from
  the TimelineView date, so the main-thread stall during scene load froze them
  and then jumped. Moving the 150 MP HEIC decode off-main (with
  kCGImageSourceShouldCacheImmediately, which is what actually relocates a lazy
  CGImage's cost) removed one stall but not the stutter; the rest is RealityKit's
  texture upload and cannot be moved. Rings are frozen at spread phases so the
  composition survives. Status line "LOADING STARMAPS…" replaces the sweep bar.
- Scene transition held a fixed 0.82 s while the swap it was masking took
  seconds, so it faded to black, revealed the OLD sky, then cut to the new one
  unmasked. WhiteoutComponent.holding now parks the overlay at full black until
  the load actually lands. Decode starts with the fade-in rather than after it.
- Fade is to black, not white: between two dark scenes a white flash slams a
  dark-adapted eye, and alpha 1 occludes either way.
- Startup restructured: first sky decodes before the immersive space opens, so
  it never comes up as empty black limbo.
- recenter() — yaw-only (pitch/roll would tilt baked stereo disparity off the
  interocular axis), snaps rather than slews (vection), auto-runs at launch.

Pipeline:
- Pod completion race in sky360/process_backdrops/neural_sr: all three polled
  /queue until idle then took `ls -t | head -1`, but the queue can read empty
  before ComfyUI registers a just-POSTed prompt — silently copying the PREVIOUS
  run's output for that scene. All three now wait for an unseen filename.
- sky360 r10: edge-clamp fill replaces mirror-tiling, noise far-field seed
  (mirror-tiled detail carried p2p 80 vs 10 blurred — most of the ghosting),
  angular FAR_FALLOFF_DEG, superellipse footprint, object branch flat fill with
  no distance falloff (falloff creates the bounded disc that outpaints into a
  rimmed porthole; fields keep it).
- stereo_synth: sub-pixel forward warp. round() quantised disparity into 13
  integer terraces per hemisphere on every scene. Also fixes a pre-existing
  inverted z-priority where the right eye let the far surface win.
- master_sr: SR_BACKEND defaults to esrgan; USDU manufactured 3.6x the edge
  roughness of a plain resample. Adds --redo.
- scripts/rerender_all.py: resumable two-phase runner with progress/ETA.

Re-rendered assets are deliberately NOT in this commit — that render is still
running and the files are mid-flight.

1	import SwiftUI
2	
3	/// App entry point. A small launcher window opens the full immersive space, which
4	/// IS the experience (no passthrough). Spec: §1, §7.
5	@main
6	struct FloatApp: App {
7	    @State private var model = AppModel()
8	
9	    // Every panel here is `Window`, not `WindowGroup`: a WindowGroup is a *template* and
10	    // `openWindow(id:)` spawns a fresh instance each call, so re-tapping "Scenes…" — or the
11	    // §7 double-pinch, which fires whenever a pinch pair lands — stacked duplicate pickers
12	    // and menus in the space. `Window` is a singleton scene: opening an already-open one
13	    // just brings it forward.
14	    var body: some Scene {
15	        Window("Float", id: "launcher") {
16	            // LauncherView stays MOUNTED under the splash rather than being swapped for
17	            // it: its `.task` is what opens the immersive space, so gating it behind
18	            // `sceneReady` would mean nothing ever loads and the splash never lifts.
19	            ZStack {
20	                LauncherView()
21	                    .environment(model)
22	                if !model.sceneReady {
23	                    SplashView().transition(.opacity)
24	                }
25	            }
26	            // Explicit size because `.contentSize` shrink-wraps to the ideal size, and
27	            // SplashView has none (it is maxWidth/maxHeight .infinity by design). Without
28	            // this the launch window collapses around the menu and the splash renders in
29	            // a sliver.
30	            .frame(width: 720, height: 520)
31	            .animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.8), value: model.sceneReady)
32	        }
33	        .windowResizability(.contentSize)
34	
35	        // Reading panel (Kindle Cloud Reader etc.) as its own window — the system gives it a
36	        // drag bar + resize + eye-level placement, so you can put it wherever you're lying.
37	        Window("Reader", id: "reader") {
38	            ReaderPanelView()
39	        }
40	        .defaultSize(width: 640, height: 900)
41	
42	        // Scene picker (§7a) — its own window so it can be opened from inside the immersive
43	        // space and left floating while iterating on a specific sky.
44	        Window("Scenes", id: "scenes") {
45	            SceneSelectorView()
46	                .environment(model)
47	        }
48	        .defaultSize(width: 520, height: 640)
49	
50	        // Entertainment sub-menu — Kindle / Music / Video.
51	        Window("Entertainment", id: "entertainment") {
52	            EntertainmentMenuView()
53	        }
54	        .defaultSize(width: 400, height: 480)
55	
56	        ImmersiveSpace(id: AppModel.immersiveSpaceID) {
57	            ImmersiveView()
58	                .environment(model)
59	        }
60	        // §1 — full immersion, everything else out of the way.
61	        .immersionStyle(selection: .constant(.full), in: .full)
62	    }
63	}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build the four test planet/moon bodies as USDZ geometry for RealityKit.

Run under Blender, not bare python:

    /Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender -b -P scripts/render_planets.py -- [--bake] [--only saturn]

WHY GEOMETRY AND NOT A PAINTED BACKDROP
    The sky HEICs sit at one near-infinite depth (depth_floor 0.94, ~0.2% baseline), so
    anything composited into the equirect has no parallax between the eyes. That is a large
    part of why the existing `saturn1` scene reads as a picture of space rather than a place.
    A body the viewer is supposed to feel near has to be real geometry with real stereo.

WHY CYCLES AND A BAKE (and only for Saturn)
    visionOS rejects RealityKit's `CustomMaterial` — only `ShaderGraphMaterial` authored in
    Reality Composer Pro, no hand-written Metal — so the app cannot render the two shadows
    that sell Saturn: the ring shadow banding the globe, and the globe's shadow thrown across
    the rings. Those get ray-traced here and baked into the colour map. Bake the LIGHTING,
    never the geometry: stereo parallax has to stay real, and a body that rotates once per
    ~10.6 h can afford frozen lighting. Jupiter, Venus and Iapetus have no self-shadowing
    feature to capture, so they ship unbaked and keep a live RealityKit light.

Stage 1 (always) exports plain textured USDZ for every body — fast, and enough to judge scale
and sharpness in the headset. Stage 2 (`--bake`) is the Saturn ring/globe shadow bake, which
is slow and the part most likely to need iterating; a stage-2 failure still leaves stage 1's
output on disk.
"""

import argparse
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import bpy  # noqa: E402  (only importable inside Blender)

SRC = Path("/Volumes/Logic Pro/FloatScratch/planets")
OUT = Path("/Volumes/Logic Pro/FloatScratch/planets/usdz")

# Sphere tessellation. 256x128 is well past what silhouette-smoothness needs at these angular
# sizes; the cost is trivial next to the textures and it keeps the limb from faceting when a
# body fills a large part of the view.
SEGMENTS, RINGS = 256, 128

# Axial tilt (degrees) applied about X so the poles do not sit dead vertical — a body lit and
# tilted reads as a world, a body square-on reads as a sticker. Venus is retrograde (177°),
# which is why its "north" ends up nearly upside down; that is correct, not a bug.
BODIES = {
    "iapetus": {"map": "iapetus_map_8192.png", "tilt": 15.5},
    "jupiter": {"map": "jupiter_map_8192.png", "tilt": 3.1},
    "saturn":  {"map": "saturn_map_8192.png",  "tilt": 26.7, "rings": True},
    "venus":   {"map": "Solarsystemscope_texture_8k_venus_surface.jpg", "tilt": 177.4},
}

# Saturn's rings, in globe radii. C ring inner edge to A ring outer edge.
RING_INNER, RING_OUTER = 1.235, 2.27
RING_ALPHA = "Solarsystemscope_texture_8k_saturn_ring_alpha.png"
RING_SEGMENTS = 512

# Sun placement. Off to one side and slightly above so there is a terminator to read depth
# from, but not so oblique that most of the body is unlit.
SUN_EULER = (0.0, 0.98, 0.60)   # radians
BAKE_SIZE = 4096


def log(msg):
    print(f"[planets] {msg}", flush=True)


def reset_scene():
    bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
    scene = bpy.context.scene
    scene.render.engine = "CYCLES"
    # Metal GPU if this machine exposes one; Cycles falls back to CPU on its own if not.
    try:
        prefs = bpy.context.preferences.addons["cycles"].preferences
        prefs.compute_device_type = "METAL"
        prefs.get_devices()
        for dev in prefs.devices:
            dev.use = True
        scene.cycles.device = "GPU"
    except Exception as exc:                      # noqa: BLE001 - informational only
        log(f"GPU unavailable ({exc}); using CPU")
    scene.cycles.samples = 256


def add_sun():
    bpy.ops.object.light_add(type="SUN", location=(0, 0, 0))
    sun = bpy.context.object
    sun.rotation_euler = SUN_EULER
    sun.data.energy = 4.0
    # A real sun is not a point at this distance, and a hard-edged ring shadow looks CG.
    # ~0.53° is the sun's actual angular diameter from Earth; from Saturn it is far smaller,
    # but a little penumbra reads better than a razor edge.
    sun.data.angle = 0.009
    return sun


def make_globe(name, map_path, tilt_deg):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_uv_sphere_add(segments=SEGMENTS, ring_count=RINGS, radius=1.0)
    globe = bpy.context.object
    globe.name = name
    bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()
    # The UV sphere primitive's default unwrap is already equirectangular (u wraps longitude,
    # v runs pole to pole), which is exactly how these maps are authored — no reprojection.
    globe.rotation_euler = (tilt_deg * 3.14159265 / 180.0, 0, 0)

    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(f"{name}_mat")
    mat.use_nodes = True
    bsdf = mat.node_tree.nodes["Principled BSDF"]
    tex = mat.node_tree.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexImage")
    tex.image = bpy.data.images.load(str(map_path))
    # Colour maps are authored in sRGB; the default guess is right for jpg but be explicit so
    # the png-vs-jpg sources cannot end up graded differently from each other.
    tex.image.colorspace_settings.name = "sRGB"
    mat.node_tree.links.new(bsdf.inputs["Base Color"], tex.outputs["Color"])
    bsdf.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = 0.9   # no specular hotspot on a rock or a cloud deck
    bsdf.inputs["Metallic"].default_value = 0.0
    globe.data.materials.append(mat)
    return globe, mat, tex


def make_rings(name):
    """Flat annulus with radial UVs.

    The SSS ring texture is a strip (8192x~500) where the X axis IS radial position, so the
    unwrap has to map u = normalised radius rather than anything the automatic unwrappers
    would produce. Building the mesh by hand is the short path to that.
    """
    import bmesh

    mesh = bpy.data.meshes.new(f"{name}_rings")
    obj = bpy.data.objects.new(f"{name}_rings", mesh)
    bpy.context.collection.objects.link(obj)

    bm = bmesh.new()
    uv_layer = bm.loops.layers.uv.new()
    import math
    inner, outer = [], []
    for i in range(RING_SEGMENTS):
        a = 2 * math.pi * i / RING_SEGMENTS
        inner.append(bm.verts.new((math.cos(a) * RING_INNER, math.sin(a) * RING_INNER, 0)))
        outer.append(bm.verts.new((math.cos(a) * RING_OUTER, math.sin(a) * RING_OUTER, 0)))
    bm.verts.ensure_lookup_table()
    for i in range(RING_SEGMENTS):
        j = (i + 1) % RING_SEGMENTS
        face = bm.faces.new((inner[i], outer[i], outer[j], inner[j]))
        # u: 0 at the inner edge, 1 at the outer edge. v is unused by a 1-D strip.
        for loop, u in zip(face.loops, (0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0)):
            loop[uv_layer].uv = (u, 0.5)
    bm.to_mesh(mesh)
    bm.free()

    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(f"{name}_rings_mat")
    mat.use_nodes = True
    mat.blend_method = "BLEND"
    bsdf = mat.node_tree.nodes["Principled BSDF"]
    tex = mat.node_tree.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexImage")

    /Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender -b -P scripts/render_planets.py -- [--bake] [--only saturn]

    The sky HEICs sit at one near-infinite depth (depth_floor 0.94, ~0.2% baseline), so
    anything composited into the equirect has no parallax between the eyes. That is a large
    part of why the existing `saturn1` scene reads as a picture of space rather than a place.
    A body the viewer is supposed to feel near has to be real geometry with real stereo.

WHY CYCLES AND A BAKE (and only for Saturn)
    visionOS rejects RealityKit's `CustomMaterial` — only `ShaderGraphMaterial` authored in
    Reality Composer Pro, no hand-written Metal — so the app cannot render the two shadows
    that sell Saturn: the ring shadow banding the globe, and the globe's shadow thrown across
    the rings. Those get ray-traced here and baked into the colour map. Bake the LIGHTING,
    never the geometry: stereo parallax has to stay real, and a body that rotates once per
    ~10.6 h can afford frozen lighting. Jupiter, Venus and Iapetus have no self-shadowing
    feature to capture, so they ship unbaked and keep a live RealityKit light.

Stage 1 (always) exports plain textured USDZ for every body — fast, and enough to judge scale
and sharpness in the headset. Stage 2 (`--bake`) is the Saturn ring/globe shadow bake, which
is slow and the part most likely to need iterating; a stage-2 failure still leaves stage 1's
output on disk.

import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

SRC = Path("/Volumes/Logic Pro/FloatScratch/planets")

# sizes; the cost is trivial next to the textures and it keeps the limb from faceting when a
# body fills a large part of the view.
SEGMENTS, RINGS = 256, 128

# Axial tilt (degrees) applied about X so the poles do not sit dead vertical — a body lit and
# tilted reads as a world, a body square-on reads as a sticker. Venus is retrograde (177°),
# which is why its "north" ends up nearly upside down; that is correct, not a bug.
BODIES = {
    "iapetus": {"map": "iapetus_map_8192.png", "tilt": 15.5},
    "jupiter": {"map": "jupiter_map_8192.png", "tilt": 3.1},
    "saturn":  {"map": "saturn_map_8192.png",  "tilt": 26.7, "rings": True},
    "venus":   {"map": "Solarsystemscope_texture_8k_venus_surface.jpg", "tilt": 177.4},

    mat.blend_method = "BLEND"

    tex = mat.node_tree.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexImage")
    tex.image = bpy.data.images.load(str(SRC / RING_ALPHA))

    mat.node_tree.links.new(bsdf.inputs["Base Color"], tex.outputs["Color"])

    log(f"wrote {path.name} ({path.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f} MB)")

102	    bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()

106

108	    mat.use_nodes = True
109	    bsdf = mat.node_tree.nodes["Principled BSDF"]
110	    tex = mat.node_tree.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexImage")
111	    tex.image = bpy.data.images.load(str(map_path))

123	    """Flat annulus with radial UVs.

135	    bm = bmesh.new()
136	    uv_layer = bm.loops.layers.uv.new()
137	    import math
138	    inner, outer = [], []
139	    for i in range(RING_SEGMENTS):
140	        a = 2 * math.pi * i / RING_SEGMENTS
141	        inner.append(bm.verts.new((math.cos(a) * RING_INNER, math.sin(a) * RING_INNER, 0)))
142	        outer.append(bm.verts.new((math.cos(a) * RING_OUTER, math.sin(a) * RING_OUTER, 0)))

144	    for i in range(RING_SEGMENTS):
145	        j = (i + 1) % RING_SEGMENTS
146	        face = bm.faces.new((inner[i], outer[i], outer[j], inner[j]))
147	        # u: 0 at the inner edge, 1 at the outer edge. v is unused by a 1-D strip.
148	        for loop, u in zip(face.loops, (0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0)):

2	"""Build the four test planet/moon bodies as USDZ geometry for RealityKit.
3	
4	Run under Blender, not bare python:
5	
6	    /Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender -b -P scripts/render_planets.py -- [--bake] [--only saturn]
7	
8	WHY GEOMETRY AND NOT A PAINTED BACKDROP
9	    The sky HEICs sit at one near-infinite depth (depth_floor 0.94, ~0.2% baseline), so
10	    anything composited into the equirect has no parallax between the eyes. That is a large
11	    part of why the existing `saturn1` scene reads as a picture of space rather than a place.
12	    A body the viewer is supposed to feel near has to be real geometry with real stereo.
13	
14	WHY CYCLES AND A BAKE (and only for Saturn)
15	    visionOS rejects RealityKit's `CustomMaterial` — only `ShaderGraphMaterial` authored in
16	    Reality Composer Pro, no hand-written Metal — so the app cannot render the two shadows
17	    that sell Saturn: the ring shadow banding the globe, and the globe's shadow thrown across
18	    the rings. Stage 2 currently bakes the FIRST of those only — the ring shadow onto the
19	    globe. The globe's shadow across the rings needs a bake target on the ring annulus, and
20	    the annulus UV here is deliberately 1-D (u = radius, v pinned) to match the strip texture,
21	    which leaves nothing to bake into. That needs a second UV set before it can work.
22	    What is baked is ray-traced here and painted into the colour map. Bake the LIGHTING,
23	    never the geometry: stereo parallax has to stay real, and a body that rotates once per
24	    ~10.6 h can afford frozen lighting. Jupiter, Venus and Iapetus have no self-shadowing
25	    feature to capture, so they ship unbaked and keep a live RealityKit light.
26	
27	Stage 1 (always) exports plain textured USDZ for every body — fast, and enough to judge scale
28	and sharpness in the headset. Stage 2 (`--bake`) is the Saturn ring/globe shadow bake, which
29	is slow and the part most likely to need iterating; a stage-2 failure still leaves stage 1's
30	output on disk.
31	"""
32	
33	import argparse
34	import os
35	import sys
36	from pathlib import Path
37	
38	import bpy  # noqa: E402  (only importable inside Blender)
39	
40	SRC = Path("/Volumes/Logic Pro/FloatScratch/planets")
41	OUT = Path("/Volumes/Logic Pro/FloatScratch/planets/usdz")
42	
43	# Sphere tessellation. 256x128 is well past what silhouette-smoothness needs at these angular
44	# sizes; the cost is trivial next to the textures and it keeps the limb from faceting when a
45	# body fills a large part of the view.
46	SEGMENTS, RINGS = 256, 128
47	
48	# Axial tilt (degrees) applied about X so the poles do not sit dead vertical — a body lit and
49	# tilted reads as a world, a body square-on reads as a sticker. Venus is retrograde (177°),
50	# which is why its "north" ends up nearly upside down; that is correct, not a bug.
51	BODIES = {
52	    "iapetus": {"map": "iapetus_map_8192.png", "tilt": 15.5},
53	    "jupiter": {"map": "jupiter_map_8192.png", "tilt": 3.1},
54	    "saturn":  {"map": "saturn_map_8192.png",  "tilt": 26.7, "rings": True},
55	    "venus":   {"map": "Solarsystemscope_texture_8k_venus_surface.jpg", "tilt": 177.4},
56	}
57	
58	# Saturn's rings, in globe radii. C ring inner edge to A ring outer edge.
59	RING_INNER, RING_OUTER = 1.235, 2.27
60	RING_ALPHA = "Solarsystemscope_texture_8k_saturn_ring_alpha.png"
61	RING_SEGMENTS = 512
62	
63	# Sun placement. Off to one side and slightly above so there is a terminator to read depth
64	# from, but not so oblique that most of the body is unlit.
65	SUN_EULER = (0.0, 0.98, 0.60)   # radians
66	BAKE_SIZE = 8192   # match the source map; 4096 halved the angular resolution the "huge vs sharp" budget assumed
67	
68	
69	def log(msg):
70	    print(f"[planets] {msg}", flush=True)
71	
72	
73	def reset_scene():
74	    bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
75	    scene = bpy.context.scene
76	    scene.render.engine = "CYCLES"
77	    # Metal GPU if this machine exposes one; Cycles falls back to CPU on its own if not.
78	    try:
79	        prefs = bpy.context.preferences.addons["cycles"].preferences
80	        prefs.compute_device_type = "METAL"
81	        prefs.get_devices()
82	        for dev in prefs.devices:
83	            dev.use = True
84	        scene.cycles.device = "GPU"
85	    except Exception as exc:                      # noqa: BLE001 - informational only
86	        log(f"GPU unavailable ({exc}); using CPU")
87	    scene.cycles.samples = 256
88	
89	
90	def add_sun():
91	    bpy.ops.object.light_add(type="SUN", location=(0, 0, 0))
92	    sun = bpy.context.object
93	    sun.rotation_euler = SUN_EULER
94	    sun.data.energy = 4.0
95	    # A real sun is not a point at this distance, and a hard-edged ring shadow looks CG.
96	    # ~0.53° is the sun's actual angular diameter from Earth; from Saturn it is far smaller,
97	    # but a little penumbra reads better than a razor edge.
98	    sun.data.angle = 0.009
99	    return sun
100	
101	
102	def make_globe(name, map_path, tilt_deg):
103	    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_uv_sphere_add(segments=SEGMENTS, ring_count=RINGS, radius=1.0)
104	    globe = bpy.context.object
105	    globe.name = name
106	    bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()
107	    # The UV sphere primitive's default unwrap is already equirectangular (u wraps longitude,
108	    # v runs pole to pole), which is exactly how these maps are authored — no reprojection.
109	    globe.rotation_euler = (tilt_deg * 3.14159265 / 180.0, 0, 0)
110	
111	    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(f"{name}_mat")
112	    mat.use_nodes = True
113	    bsdf = mat.node_tree.nodes["Principled BSDF"]
114	    tex = mat.node_tree.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexImage")
115	    tex.image = bpy.data.images.load(str(map_path))
116	    # Colour maps are authored in sRGB; the default guess is right for jpg but be explicit so
117	    # the png-vs-jpg sources cannot end up graded differently from each other.
118	    tex.image.colorspace_settings.name = "sRGB"
119	    mat.node_tree.links.new(bsdf.inputs["Base Color"], tex.outputs["Color"])
120	    bsdf.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = 0.9   # no specular hotspot on a rock or a cloud deck
121	    bsdf.inputs["Metallic"].default_value = 0.0
122	    globe.data.materials.append(mat)
123	    return globe, mat, tex
124	
125	
126	def make_rings(name):
127	    """Flat annulus with radial UVs.
128	
129	    The SSS ring texture is a strip (8192x~500) where the X axis IS radial position, so the
130	    unwrap has to map u = normalised radius rather than anything the automatic unwrappers
131	    would produce. Building the mesh by hand is the short path to that.
132	    """
133	    import bmesh
134	
135	    mesh = bpy.data.meshes.new(f"{name}_rings")
136	    obj = bpy.data.objects.new(f"{name}_rings", mesh)
137	    bpy.context.collection.objects.link(obj)
138	
139	    bm = bmesh.new()
140	    uv_layer = bm.loops.layers.uv.new()
141	    import math
142	    inner, outer = [], []
143	    for i in range(RING_SEGMENTS):
144	        a = 2 * math.pi * i / RING_SEGMENTS
145	        inner.append(bm.verts.new((math.cos(a) * RING_INNER, math.sin(a) * RING_INNER, 0)))
146	        outer.append(bm.verts.new((math.cos(a) * RING_OUTER, math.sin(a) * RING_OUTER, 0)))
147	    bm.verts.ensure_lookup_table()
148	    for i in range(RING_SEGMENTS):
149	        j = (i + 1) % RING_SEGMENTS
150	        face = bm.faces.new((inner[i], outer[i], outer[j], inner[j]))
151	        # u: 0 at the inner edge, 1 at the outer edge. v is unused by a 1-D strip.
152	        for loop, u in zip(face.loops, (0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0)):
153	            loop[uv_layer].uv = (u, 0.5)
154	    bm.to_mesh(mesh)
155	    bm.free()
156	
157	    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(f"{name}_rings_mat")
158	    mat.use_nodes = True
159	    mat.blend_method = "BLEND"
160	    bsdf = mat.node_tree.nodes["Principled BSDF"]
161	    tex = mat.node_tree.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexImage")
162	    tex.image = bpy.data.images.load(str(SRC / RING_ALPHA))
163	    tex.extension = "EXTEND"   # never wrap: sampling past the outer edge must not fetch the C ring
164	    mat.node_tree.links.new(bsdf.inputs["Base Color"], tex.outputs["Color"])

+/// The player is not `Sendable` and its playback methods are `nonisolated async`, so a
+/// `@MainActor` caller awaiting `player.play()` is *sending* a non-Sendable value across an
+/// isolation boundary — which Swift 6 rejects outright. Reaching for `.shared` INSIDE a

+/// nothing is ever sent. Same singleton either way; this is about where it is touched from.
+/// It has to be the shared instance: that is the queue the system Now Playing controls and the
+/// audio session are attached to, and a second player would fight this one for both.
+    static func play<T: PlayableMusicItem>(_ item: T) async throws {

Entertainment: real browser, in-app Music, honest Watch labels; planet USDZ

Browser (replaces the single-page Kindle reader, WebReaderPanel.swift):
- Tabs, each keeping its own WKWebView for the window's lifetime so switching
  preserves scroll position, form state and JS context.
- Session restore — reopens the tabs that were open, on the tab that was in
  front. That IS the "default to the last page used": no home page needed.
- History with search and clear, deduped by URL so repeat visits update one row
  instead of stacking forty copies of the same page.
- Address bar that takes a URL or a search. "Plausibly a URL" = has a scheme, or
  has a dot and no spaces, which keeps `read.amazon.com` working bare without
  turning `swift concurrency` into a hostname.
- One shared persistent data store across all tabs, so a passkey/Optic ID login
  happens once and survives relaunch.
- target=_blank links load in the requesting tab rather than silently doing
  nothing, which is the usual "this link is broken" bug in an embedded web view.

iCloud Tabs: NOT possible. Safari's iCloud tab list has no public API. Handoff
(NSUserActivityTypeBrowsingWeb) is the supported equivalent and is wired up: with
Safari frontmost on a Mac or iPhone, Float appears in the Dock and opens that
page in a new tab.

Music: MusicKit, played in-process via ApplicationMusicPlayer — library
playlists/albums, catalog search, now-playing transport. Launching Music.app tore
down the immersive space (visionOS makes it exclusive), so changing a track meant
leaving deep space. Playback state is read from the player's own ObservableObject
rather than mirrored, since it changes for reasons this app never sees.
REQUIRES the MusicKit capability on the Ash4d.Float App ID at developer.apple.com
— code alone cannot enable it.

Watch: the Apple TV app's library has no public API; its titles are FairPlay-
protected and decrypt only inside that app. Rather than a "TV Library" button
that could only fail, the section names its two working sources — local video
from Photos, and tv.apple.com/streaming sites via the browser.

def render_preview(objects, name, r_eff):
    """Camera render of the body for the triage page.

    2:1 to match the card aspect on triage.html — the grid crops anything else and would
    slice the rings off Saturn. Distance is derived from the body's effective radius rather
    than hand-set per body, so Iapetus and ringed Saturn frame the same way.

    scene.render.image_settings.file_format = "PNG"

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Build the four test planet/moon bodies as USDZ geometry for RealityKit.
3	
4	Run under Blender, not bare python:
5	
6	    /Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender -b -P scripts/render_planets.py -- [--bake] [--only saturn]
7	
8	WHY GEOMETRY AND NOT A PAINTED BACKDROP
9	    The sky HEICs sit at one near-infinite depth (depth_floor 0.94, ~0.2% baseline), so
10	    anything composited into the equirect has no parallax between the eyes. That is a large
11	    part of why the existing `saturn1` scene reads as a picture of space rather than a place.
12	    A body the viewer is supposed to feel near has to be real geometry with real stereo.
13	
14	WHY CYCLES AND A BAKE (and only for Saturn)
15	    visionOS rejects RealityKit's `CustomMaterial` — only `ShaderGraphMaterial` authored in
16	    Reality Composer Pro, no hand-written Metal — so the app cannot render the two shadows
17	    that sell Saturn: the ring shadow banding the globe, and the globe's shadow thrown across
18	    the rings. Stage 2 currently bakes the FIRST of those only — the ring shadow onto the
19	    globe. The globe's shadow across the rings needs a bake target on the ring annulus, and
20	    the annulus UV here is deliberately 1-D (u = radius, v pinned) to match the strip texture,
21	    which leaves nothing to bake into. That needs a second UV set before it can work.
22	    What is baked is ray-traced here and painted into the colour map. Bake the LIGHTING,
23	    never the geometry: stereo parallax has to stay real, and a body that rotates once per
24	    ~10.6 h can afford frozen lighting. Jupiter, Venus and Iapetus have no self-shadowing
25	    feature to capture, so they ship unbaked and keep a live RealityKit light.
26	
27	Stage 1 (always) exports plain textured USDZ for every body — fast, and enough to judge scale
28	and sharpness in the headset. Stage 2 (`--bake`) is the Saturn ring/globe shadow bake, which
29	is slow and the part most likely to need iterating; a stage-2 failure still leaves stage 1's
30	output on disk.
31	"""
32	
33	import argparse
34	import os
35	import sys
36	from pathlib import Path
37	
38	import bpy  # noqa: E402  (only importable inside Blender)
39	
40	SRC = Path("/Volumes/Logic Pro/FloatScratch/planets")
41	OUT = Path("/Volumes/Logic Pro/FloatScratch/planets/usdz")
42	# Previews live in the repo (small) so triage.html can reference them like the sky
43	# thumbnails; the USDZ themselves stay on the scratch volume.
44	PREV = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "upscale" / "planet_prev"
45	
46	# Sphere tessellation. 256x128 is well past what silhouette-smoothness needs at these angular
47	# sizes; the cost is trivial next to the textures and it keeps the limb from faceting when a
48	# body fills a large part of the view.
49	SEGMENTS, RINGS = 256, 128
50	
51	# Axial tilt (degrees) applied about X so the poles do not sit dead vertical — a body lit and
52	# tilted reads as a world, a body square-on reads as a sticker. Venus is retrograde (177°),
53	# which is why its "north" ends up nearly upside down; that is correct, not a bug.
54	BODIES = {
55	    "iapetus": {"map": "iapetus_map_8192.png", "tilt": 15.5},
56	    "jupiter": {"map": "jupiter_map_8192.png", "tilt": 3.1},
57	    "saturn":  {"map": "saturn_map_8192.png",  "tilt": 26.7, "rings": True},
58	    "venus":   {"map": "Solarsystemscope_texture_8k_venus_surface.jpg", "tilt": 177.4},
59	}
60	
61	# Saturn's rings, in globe radii. C ring inner edge to A ring outer edge.
62	RING_INNER, RING_OUTER = 1.235, 2.27
63	RING_ALPHA = "Solarsystemscope_texture_8k_saturn_ring_alpha.png"
64	RING_SEGMENTS = 512
65	
66	# Sun placement. Off to one side and slightly above so there is a terminator to read depth
67	# from, but not so oblique that most of the body is unlit.
68	SUN_EULER = (0.0, 0.98, 0.60)   # radians
69	BAKE_SIZE = 8192   # match the source map; 4096 halved the angular resolution the "huge vs sharp" budget assumed
70	
71	
72	def log(msg):
73	    print(f"[planets] {msg}", flush=True)
74	
75	
76	def reset_scene():
77	    bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
78	    scene = bpy.context.scene
79	    scene.render.engine = "CYCLES"
80	    # Metal GPU if this machine exposes one; Cycles falls back to CPU on its own if not.
81	    try:
82	        prefs = bpy.context.preferences.addons["cycles"].preferences
83	        prefs.compute_device_type = "METAL"
84	        prefs.get_devices()
85	        for dev in prefs.devices:
86	            dev.use = True
87	        scene.cycles.device = "GPU"
88	    except Exception as exc:                      # noqa: BLE001 - informational only
89	        log(f"GPU unavailable ({exc}); using CPU")
90	    scene.cycles.samples = 256
91	
92	
93	def add_sun():
94	    bpy.ops.object.light_add(type="SUN", location=(0, 0, 0))
95	    sun = bpy.context.object
96	    sun.rotation_euler = SUN_EULER
97	    sun.data.energy = 4.0
98	    # A real sun is not a point at this distance, and a hard-edged ring shadow looks CG.
99	    # ~0.53° is the sun's actual angular diameter from Earth; from Saturn it is far smaller,
100	    # but a little penumbra reads better than a razor edge.
101	    sun.data.angle = 0.009
102	    return sun
103	
104	
105	def make_globe(name, map_path, tilt_deg):
106	    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_uv_sphere_add(segments=SEGMENTS, ring_count=RINGS, radius=1.0)
107	    globe = bpy.context.object
108	    globe.name = name
109	    bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()
110	    # The UV sphere primitive's default unwrap is already equirectangular (u wraps longitude,
111	    # v runs pole to pole), which is exactly how these maps are authored — no reprojection.
112	    globe.rotation_euler = (tilt_deg * 3.14159265 / 180.0, 0, 0)
113	
114	    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(f"{name}_mat")
115	    mat.use_nodes = True
116	    bsdf = mat.node_tree.nodes["Principled BSDF"]
117	    tex = mat.node_tree.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexImage")
118	    tex.image = bpy.data.images.load(str(map_path))
119	    # Colour maps are authored in sRGB; the default guess is right for jpg but be explicit so
120	    # the png-vs-jpg sources cannot end up graded differently from each other.
121	    tex.image.colorspace_settings.name = "sRGB"
122	    mat.node_tree.links.new(bsdf.inputs["Base Color"], tex.outputs["Color"])
123	    bsdf.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = 0.9   # no specular hotspot on a rock or a cloud deck
124	    bsdf.inputs["Metallic"].default_value = 0.0
125	    globe.data.materials.append(mat)
126	    return globe, mat, tex
127	
128	
129	def make_rings(name):
130	    """Flat annulus with radial UVs.
131	
132	    The SSS ring texture is a strip (8192x~500) where the X axis IS radial position, so the
133	    unwrap has to map u = normalised radius rather than anything the automatic unwrappers
134	    would produce. Building the mesh by hand is the short path to that.
135	    """
136	    import bmesh
137	
138	    mesh = bpy.data.meshes.new(f"{name}_rings")
139	    obj = bpy.data.objects.new(f"{name}_rings", mesh)
140	    bpy.context.collection.objects.link(obj)
141	
142	    bm = bmesh.new()
143	    uv_layer = bm.loops.layers.uv.new()
144	    import math
145	    inner, outer = [], []
146	    for i in range(RING_SEGMENTS):
147	        a = 2 * math.pi * i / RING_SEGMENTS
148	        inner.append(bm.verts.new((math.cos(a) * RING_INNER, math.sin(a) * RING_INNER, 0)))
149	        outer.append(bm.verts.new((math.cos(a) * RING_OUTER, math.sin(a) * RING_OUTER, 0)))
150	    bm.verts.ensure_lookup_table()
151	    for i in range(RING_SEGMENTS):
152	        j = (i + 1) % RING_SEGMENTS
153	        face = bm.faces.new((inner[i], outer[i], outer[j], inner[j]))
154	        # u: 0 at the inner edge, 1 at the outer edge. v is unused by a 1-D strip.
155	        for loop, u in zip(face.loops, (0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0)):
156	            loop[uv_layer].uv = (u, 0.5)
157	    bm.to_mesh(mesh)
158	    bm.free()
159	
160	    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(f"{name}_rings_mat")
161	    mat.use_nodes = True
162	    mat.blend_method = "BLEND"
163	    bsdf = mat.node_tree.nodes["Principled BSDF"]
164	    tex = mat.node_tree.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexImage")

The 8192 bake is still running (it takes several minutes). Everything else is done and committed. Current state while I wait for it:

**Committed and pushed** (`e4b2d25`, `7e82864`):
- Splash stutter fix + scene-transition race fix
- The whole entertainment rework

**Entertainment — what you asked for vs. what's possible:**

| Ask | Status |
|---|---|
| Browser with tabs | Done |
| Opens to last page used | Done — restores all tabs *and* which was in front, so it comes back to the Kindle without being told |
| History | Done — searchable, dedup'd by URL, clearable |
| iCloud tabs | **Not possible** — no public API; Safari's iCloud tab list is private to Safari |
| Music embedded | Done — MusicKit, plays in-process |
| Video from TV app library | **Not possible** — FairPlay content decrypts only inside the TV app |
| Relabel to show content source | Done |

For iCloud tabs I wired up the sanctioned equivalent: **Handoff**. With Safari frontmost on your Mac or iPhone, Float appears in the Dock and opening it lands that page in a new tab. It's the page you're on rather than the full tab list, but it's the actual supported path.

For the TV library, the section now names its two working sources instead of offering a button that could only fail: local video from Photos, and `tv.apple.com`/streaming sites via the browser (which is the route you suggested). Worth knowing: whether `tv.apple.com` will actually play DRM'd video inside a WKWebView is untested — some services refuse non-Safari web views.

**One thing needs you, not code:** in-app Music requires the **MusicKit capability** on the `Ash4d.Float` App ID at developer.apple.com (Identifiers → App Services → MusicKit). Without it authorization succeeds but every request comes back empty.

**Planets:** all four exported as USDZ geometry. The Cycles bake genuinely works — the ring shadow is visibly banded across Saturn's globe. Previews are rendered and the triage splice is written and tested (purely additive, your 50 existing cards and their marks untouched). I'll run the final splice and commit once the 8192 bake lands.

Two judgement calls I made that you may want to overrule: the sun angle (I settled on 45° for a visible terminator after a first pass left three-quarters of the globe black), and Iapetus using the **mono** mosaic — the 8192 map is greyscale, so the Cassini colour map you downloaded isn't being used yet.
